summary: Activity feed for dashboards: a vertical timeline with avatar, author, action, time in a <time> element and a decorative colored status dot.
whenToUse: Showing the latest user or system actions (publications, comments, approvals).
Providing recent context next to dashboard KPIs.
whenNotToUse: Steps of a process or the history of a single object: use Timeline.
Notifications that require action: use Toast, Alert or a notification center.
Long logs that need filtering: use DataTable with pagination.

props.name: title
props.description: Card title; also provides the list's accessible name.

props.name: items
props.description: Activities in reverse chronological order; time is preformatted text, dateTime the ISO value for <time>.

props.name: footer
props.description: Link to the full log, or a note.

props.name: emptyState
props.description: Shown instead of the list when items is empty.

inherits: HTML attributes of <div> (id, style, data-*, aria-*).
accessibility: <ul> list named by the title (aria-labelledby); each item is a complete “author + action” sentence.
Avatar, status dot and timeline line are decorative (aria-hidden): the author's name is visible text.
The tone carries no exclusive information: state the outcome in the action (“failed”, “approved”).
The time uses <time dateTime> for an unambiguous reading.
responsive: Text and time wrap; avatar and line stay aligned to the start of the row (RTL support via logical properties).
customization: Tokens: --dc-look-radius-container, feedback colors for status dots, --dc-color-border-subtle for the line.
commonMistakes: Conveying the outcome through the dot color alone.
Omitting dateTime with relative times (“yesterday”): the machine value helps assistive technologies and extensions.
Making the whole row clickable: put explicit links in the action.

examples.name: WithTones
examples.title: Tones and links
examples.description: All tones, links in the action, and a footer.

limits: Times are not formatted by the component: pass already localized text (e.g. with RelativeTime).
No built-in pagination or progressive loading.
